clue.text: 12 sheep delay broadcast

definitions.note: a cross-reference: the answer at 12 across, the famous long sleeper, stands in as the definition

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone counting sheep to fall asleep, with a radio broadcast somehow held up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 12 across, RIP VAN WINKLE, the man who slept twenty years; counting sheep is the joke that ties the surface to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip Van Winkle is the classic example of a drowsy person, one who dozed for decades in the story.

clue.text: Primarily, spiritualist ultimately finding ihsān?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A spiritual seeker who, in the end, attains ihsān, the Islamic ideal of perfect worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Ihsān is the Arabic term for spiritual excellence, doing good as though seeing God. The whole clue both spells the answer and describes it, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufism is Islam's mystical tradition, whose followers strive inwardly toward ihsān, the state of perfected devotion.

clue.text: Beauty magazine, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: a word that reads the same from either direction looks identical whichever way it is viewed

parts.note: a well-known fashion and beauty title

explanation.surface: A glossy beauty magazine that looks good from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate wordplay: the clue simply adds that the title reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elle is an internationally published women's magazine covering fashion, cosmetics and style.

clue.text: Granadilla spread one consumed on Friday. Peeled? Quite

indicators.note: in a down clue, one part placed on another sits above it, so the parts follow one another
what is consumed is swallowed up, so one piece ends up inside another

parts.note: to pass on news or a disease is to spread it
the Roman numeral for one
a standard abbreviation of the day

indicators.note: peeling strips away the skin, leaving only the inner flesh of the word

parts.note: the word with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone eating granadilla, peeled, at the end of the week, and finding it rather good.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stops break the clue into chunks so that 'on Friday' reads as a time, when 'on' actually stacks the first word above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Granadilla is another name for the fruit of the passion flower vine, especially the sweet yellow variety.

clue.text: Constituents of Antioch, an overseas principality once

indicators.note: constituents are the parts that make something up, so the answer is made of letters already in the phrase

parts.note: runs from the end of the city name into the last word

explanation.surface: The people of Antioch, an ancient city abroad that was once a princely state.
explanation.walkthrough: Antioch was itself a crusader principality, which makes the surface plausible; the answer is the German state instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover was a German electorate and later kingdom ruled by princes, whose house gave Britain its Georgian monarchs.

clue.text: I tucked into tea, not ardently consumed

indicators.note: something tucked into a thing is pushed inside it
ardent feeling is passionate and agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into afternoon tea without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' looks like eating, in keeping with the definition, but it is the instruction to place the single letter inside the rearranged words.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into something is to use it up or wear it away, so the phrasal verb matches consumed.

clue.text: Employs guessers now and then

indicators.note: something done now and then happens at intervals, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: An employer who hires people who occasionally guess.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters rather than the odd ones is the right choice here; the odd ones give nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is simply to make use of it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Bouillon for starters: pungent, inedible, the French food not yet eaten?

parts.note: bouillon is a clear broth or stock

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning of a meal, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the two adjectives
French plural word for the

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu where the soup starter is strong-smelling and inedible, so the French food goes uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For starters' looks attached to the bouillon as a soup course, but it governs the following two words. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockpiles are reserves built up for later, so food in store has not yet been consumed.

clue.text: No end of fish and beef

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: small silvery fish with a bright stripe along each flank

explanation.surface: A menu offering plenty of fish and beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' reads as 'lots of', but it means cut the last letter. Silversides are a family of small fish; silverside is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter, often salted.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a lean joint taken from the outer thigh of cattle, used for roasting or corned meat.

clue.text: Traditional musician's fiddle enthralling ol' Kansas

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece holds others within it

parts.note: to fiddle with something is to finger it
taken as written, minus the apostrophe
the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A country fiddler's playing captivating the folks of old Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' wants to be the violin, fitting the musician; it is the verb meaning to touch idly. KS is the US postal code for Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk singer performs traditional songs handed down within a community, so is a musician of tradition.

clue.text: Fossil fuel in eyeliner, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told reaches us by ear, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: kohl is a dark powder used to line the eyes

explanation.surface: A rumour that some eyeliner contains fossil fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Kohl, the black eye cosmetic, is pronounced exactly like the fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a combustible rock formed from ancient plant remains, the classic example of a fossil fuel.

clue.text: The raw bananas: I try a dish, but …

definitions.note: a noun phrase from the idiom 'in the raw', meaning naked

indicators.note: to go bananas is to go crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner hesitantly sampling a dish of raw bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The raw' looks like an adjective describing uncooked bananas; it is the definition, from 'in the raw'. The trailing ellipsis lets 'but' feed the letters while the sentence trails off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the raw and being in your birthday suit are both jokey idioms for naked skin.

clue.text: Somnolent type to tear open vehicle with seafood

parts.note: to rip is to tear
a van is a road vehicle
a winkle is a small edible sea snail

explanation.surface: A sleepy person trying to break into a delivery van full of shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Winkles are periwinkles, small sea snails eaten in Britain, often from seaside stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: In Washington Irving's tale, Rip Van Winkle sleeps for twenty years, making his name a byword for drowsiness.

clue.text: Vulgar wiseacre's teaching aids

parts.note: flash means ostentatious or showy in a vulgar way
a card is a joker or wag, and the possessive supplies the final letter

explanation.surface: A crude know-it-all's classroom materials.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks possessive but provides the plural ending. A card is an old-fashioned word for a joker or amusing person.
explanation.definitionFit: Flash cards bear words or pictures held up by a teacher, a standard classroom tool for drills.

clue.text: Bespoke material old duke ordered

indicators.note: things that are ordered are arranged, so the letters are put in a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
a standard abbreviation of old
a standard abbreviation of duke

explanation.surface: An elderly duke commissioning custom fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' fits the surface as commissioning bespoke cloth, but it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke is the traditional British term for clothing cut to an individual customer's measurements.

clue.text: A little unclear, nervous beginner

indicators.note: a little of something is just a part of it, so the answer is a part of the phrase

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A novice who is slightly confused and anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little unclear' reads as slightly confused, but 'a little' signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone just starting to acquire a skill, such as a novice driver.

clue.text: Gets in boats to resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting the letters in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers boarding boats bound for a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday destination; read as re-sort it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it, a direct synonym of the verb gets.

clue.text: Spend a lot, swell place obtained

indicators.note: what is obtained is taken in, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea
a standard abbreviation of place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone paying a fortune once they have bought a fancy property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as the slang adjective for excellent, describing the place; it is the noun for a rising wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money freely and extravagantly on a treat.

clue.text: Artist representing Creole? Good

indicators.note: to represent something is to present it in another form, so the letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a standard abbreviation of good

explanation.surface: A painter depicting a Creole subject, and the result is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representing' fits a painter depicting someone, but it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance, famous for elongated figures.

clue.text: Go Dutch, splash out, save penny — stroke of luck!

indicators.note: save in the sense of except or but for means a part is excluded from the word

parts.note: taken as written
a standard abbreviation of Dutch
to splash out is to spend lavishly
P is the abbreviation for a British penny

explanation.surface: Advice on sharing the bill, splurging and thrift, ending in a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go Dutch' reads as the idiom for splitting a bill, but the two words separate. 'Save' looks like thrift; it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected welcome event, as if sent from heaven, so a stroke of good fortune.

clue.text: Slack-jawed at first, getting affectionate with royal

indicators.note: what comes at first is at the beginning, so only opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words
a king is a royal

explanation.surface: Someone's jaw dropping on seeing a person get cosy with a member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' seems to attach to slack-jawed before it, but it governs the three words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawking is staring stupidly with an open mouth, exactly the look of being slack-jawed.

clue.text: I saw Gary race around roads

indicators.note: racing around is moving in every direction, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A witness watching Gary speed through the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like the verb of the scene but is part of the letters; 'around' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriageway is the British term for the part of a road vehicles drive on, as in dual carriageway.

clue.text: Spy giving up date of birth (including name)

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom upward
to include something is to take it inside

parts.note: the standard initials used on forms
a standard abbreviation of name

explanation.surface: An agent under interrogation revealing a birth date and identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving up' reads as surrendering information, but in a down clue it turns the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is Ian Fleming's fictional secret agent, the most famous fictional spy.

clue.text: Wife avoiding insects and snakes

indicators.note: what avoids something keeps clear of it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: wasps are stinging insects
a standard abbreviation of wife

explanation.surface: A wife steering clear of creepy-crawlies and serpents.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife and the stinging insects share a first letter, which is what goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous vipers, the kind associated with Cleopatra's death.

clue.text: Highway travelled by horse noisily

indicators.note: something done noisily is heard, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: past tense of riding on horseback

explanation.surface: A clattering horse ride along a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense of ride, said out loud, matches the word for a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A highway is a main public route for travel, a type of thoroughfare built for traffic.

clue.text: Fastidious Everyman given time: 'silly not to deliver'

indicators.note: not means without, so a portion is taken away

parts.note: the setter refers to himself
a standard abbreviation of time
silly means absurd or laughable
to deliver from is to rid of

explanation.surface: A fussy setter given a deadline, saying it would be foolish not to hand over the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often clue themselves as ME; here the puzzle's own name does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Meticulous describes someone extremely careful about detail, the same as being fussy or fastidious.

clue.text: Egyptian city where god's rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the king of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A city in Egypt where a deity is spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, joining the god to the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is a port city in Egypt at the southern end of the famous canal.

clue.text: Ungodliest, harrowing: together they circle the world

indicators.note: a harrow breaks up and churns soil, so the letters are broken up and turned over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The most wicked people, in a distressing scene, joining forces to encircle the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrowing' reads as distressing; it is the farm sense of churning that rearranges. The definition is a descriptive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of longitude are meridians running pole to pole, and as a set they ring the entire globe.
